A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTG research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data generation, classifier generalization, uncertainty-detection and ablation results, including ImageNet-LT experiments in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports synthetic-data efficiency and distribution-quality findings.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix A.1 newly describes a total-uncertainty guidance variant using the first term of Equation 4, alongside the existing epistemic formulation. The head architecture, LTG sampling update and introspection pipeline remain unchanged. The text does not establish that this variant replaces the guidance underlying the retained benchmark tables.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Caltech101, Cars, Flowers, Pets, ImageNet-100, ImageNet-A, ImageNet-V2 and ImageNet-LT coverage. Moving ImageNet-LT from v1 Appendix A.1 to v2 Section 4.2 adds no dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, the Universal Guidance comparison, and the ImageNet-LT comparison moved from Table 4 to Table 3. Newly cited diffusion methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Section 3.1 adds a within-class synthetic-versus-real and between-class real-versus-real comparison using FID and generative precision/recall. FID already appeared in v1's intermediate-state analysis, but this comparison and precision/recall evaluation are additional. Existing classification splits, architectures and training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of synthetic-data efficiency versus GIF, generated-data distribution retention, and total uncertainty versus epistemic or aleatoric guidance alone. These additions are reported mainly in prose. The existing continued-training, guidance-weight, head-count and intermediate-state analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that classification results are averaged over three runs and retain the same plotted uncertainty displays. v2 adds no run-count changes, seed disclosures, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. v2 Section 4.1 newly reports exceeding GIF performance using 20%, 25%, 30% and 23% of its synthetic-data volume for Caltech, Cars, Flowers and Pets, respectively. Section 3.1 adds qualitative FID and precision/recall comparisons, while Appendix A.1 reports slightly better generalization with total-uncertainty guidance.

T1.justification: The uncertainty decomposition, diffusion equations, LTG update and appendix mathematical expressions are retained. The total-uncertainty discussion refers to an existing term in Equation 4; no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim of more than fourfold synthetic-data efficiency versus GIF and emphasizes data efficiency in the conclusion. The three central contributions remain the Epistemic Head, LTG and Longtail Introspection; mentioning VLM analysis in the abstract clarifies an existing contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains guidance-weight selection for retaining class identity, interprets total uncertainty as targeting both manifold edges and decision boundaries, and adds a computational explanation for earlier noisy-state classifier guidance. Its new Impact Statement also cautions against deployment overreliance and calls for evaluation on non-synthetic data.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 newly documents guidance-weight selection using reduced but nonzero desired-class probability and increased longtail signal. Appendix A.1 identifies the expression used for total-uncertainty guidance. Previously disclosed optimizers, schedules, sampling settings, hardware and introspection prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Song et al. (2023), Dou and Song (2024), Um and Ye (2024), and Kynkäänniemi et al. (2019). It additionally identifies diffusion posterior sampling as closely related and mentions minority-sample generation, modestly expanding the existing positioning.

P1.justification: v2 moves the ImageNet-LT section into the main experiments, adds Section 3.1 and an Impact Statement, and renumbers subsequent material. Abstract, conclusion and explanatory passages receive localized edits; most of the original narrative is retained.

P2.justification: The ImageNet-LT table moves into the main text and exchanges numbering with the introspection table. Captions for Figures 1, 2 and 6 are expanded, appendix displays are repositioned, and Figure 18 is resized. These are limited presentation changes to largely retained displays.

improvement.justification: v2 makes guidance selection more explicit, adds useful synthetic-data efficiency findings, improves related-work coverage and integrates the existing ImageNet-LT evidence into the main narrative. These are modest gains: the principal results remain unchanged, and the new distribution and total-uncertainty comparisons lack numerical breakdowns and sufficient procedural detail for a substantial evidential improvement.
